title: Feedback Mechanisms: Positive and Negative Practice Exam
description: Recall and guided drill for Feedback Mechanisms: Positive and Negative.

questions.question: What makes a feedback loop a negative feedback loop?
options: The response reverses the original change.
The response always stops the body.
questions.explanation: Negative feedback reverses movement away from the target range.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly traces a feedback loop?
options: stimulus -> receptor -> control center -> effector -> response
response -> no stimulus -> no sensor -> no result
control center -> no information -> no change -> no response
questions.explanation: A feedback loop starts with a detected stimulus and ends with a response.

questions.question: The body structure or tissue that carries out a response is called an ________.
Positive feedback amplifies a change until a process reaches an endpoint.
questions.explanation: Positive feedback drives a process forward.

questions.question: Explain why sweating when hot is negative feedback.
questions.correctAnswer: Sweating is negative feedback because it reduces the original temperature increase by helping the body lose heat.
questions.explanation: The answer should mention reversal of the original change.

questions.question: Which is an example of positive feedback?
options: contractions during childbirth becoming stronger until delivery
insulin lowering blood glucose after a meal
questions.explanation: Childbirth contractions intensify until the endpoint.

questions.question: Negative feedback is called negative because it is bad for the body.
questions.explanation: Negative means reversing the change, not bad.

questions.question: Name the stimulus and effector in body temperature control when a person becomes too hot.
questions.correctAnswer: The stimulus is rising body temperature; effectors include sweat glands and skin blood vessels.
questions.explanation: The answer should identify both parts.
